Describes fundamentals of the physical therapy patient care management process, clinical decision making model, and tests and measures across the disablement model. Students develop history-taking skills, conduct a review of systems, organize physical examination sequence, conduct gait analysis, and apply fundamental patient care mobility skills including gait training and assisted transfers.   Requisites: PT 7030   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture, 3.0 laboratory  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Given patient scenarios, the student will identify and distinguish between pathology, systems involved with relevant impairments, the functional limitation, the disability, and the handicap.The student will analyze abnormal gait patterns, identify the deviations, hypothesize the potential impairments, and apply the appropriate tests and measures to confirm hypotheses.The student will analyze the effect of various lower extremity impairments on the ability to walk and predict the deviations expected during gait.The student will begin to critically appraise measures based upon validity and reliability.The student will compare various disablement vs enablement models.The student will demonstrate competence in assisted patient care skills (bed mobility, transfers, gait training, wheelchair) by selecting the appropriate technique per patient needs and implement the technique accurately and safely.The student will demonstrate/perform safely and effectively the examination skills/tests and measures of the major systems (Cardiopulmonary, Musculoskeletal, Neuromuscular, Integumentary, Mental Status).The student will develop a basic plan-of-care that will address the generated hypotheses.The student will differentiate between pathology, impairment, functional limitation, and disability and as they relate to patient evaluation, diagnosis, prognosis, intervention, and outcome.The student will discuss the influence of treatment settings and the anticipated post-physical therapy discharge environment on the clinical decision-making process especially prognosis.The student will distinguish between and categorize measurements used in physical therapy in terms of the disablement model and the type of data generated by the measure.The student will employ the framework for evaluation using the Hypothesis Oriented Algorithm for Clinicians decision-making model.The student will explain the levels of the continuum of care and the role of physical therapy in each level.The student will explain the purpose of, components of, and relationships among the history, systems review and physical examination.The student will explain the role and use of The Guide to Physical Therapist Practice.The student will generate hypotheses regarding the cause of the dysfunction based upon the completed history and physical examination.The student will perform a patient history applying a variety of techniques to gather data that will successfully generate hypotheses to inform the physical examination, physical therapy diagnosis and anticipated outcome.The student will perform observational gait analysis including tasks, phases, critical events, muscle activation, and kinematic profile using video and in-class observation.The student will teach colleagues (classmates) how to perform an assigned basic patient care mobility skill (such as crutch fitting) using demonstration and written handout that meets their education needs.Using the content and skills learned in lab along with the other courses of PT 7030, the student will organize and implement a basic physical examination that addresses the major systems and overall functional limitations.

course_name: Clinical Skills and Examination II: Foundations
description: This course presents fundamentals of the physical therapy patient care management process, clinical decision making model, and tests and measures across the disablement model.  Normal/pathological  gait and posture biomechanics will be discussed.   Requisites: PT 7031 and PT 7032   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to apply the fundamentals of the physical therapy patient/client management process and clinical decision making maodel throughout the continuum of patient care.The student will be able to appropriately choose the following components of the physical therapy examination sequence that need to be performed including obtaining a subjective and medical history, review of systems, and systems screen.The student will be able to identify probable patient impairments in body structure and function, and activity/participation restrictions based on a patient’s subjective history.The student will be able to evaluate the findings of the patient screening and examination in order to make appropriate decisions regarding intervention, need for further examination, referral and/or co-treatment.The student will be able to hypothesize causes and efects of postural/alignment positions and abnormalities in both sitting and standing and the impact this has on function.The student will be able to develop postural interventions and position adjustments to make static positions and movement effective, efficient, and non-harmful for you and for paitent/clients.The student will be able to identify the characteristics of normal gait including spatial and temporal characteristics, joint motions and muscle actions.The student will be able to choose appropriate clinical tests/measures learned in PT 7031/7032 in order to identify musculoskeletal impairments that may be the result of or have led to the gait analysis findings.The student will be able to explain the differences between various levels of mobility, weight-bearing and assistance used in patient care skills.The student will be able to choose an appropriate assistive device to facilitate transfers and the functional tasks of gait.

course_name: Clinical Skills and Examination II: Applications
description: This course will focus on the development of the fundamental skills involved with physical therapy patient care management. Emphasis will be placed on patient examination and treatment techniques related to patient mobility, transfers, posture, gait training, and activities of daily living. Kinematic and kinetic motion analysis will be integrated into the evaluation process.   Requisites: PT 7031 and PT 7032   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to perform, in a timely manner, the following components of the physical therapy examination: Subjective examination and medical history and a review of systems.The student will be able to perform, appropriately, a systems screen (cardiopulmonary, musculoskeletal, integumentary, neuromuscular, and mental status screen) and interpret results.The student will be able to develop hypotheses of potential impairments in body structure and function based on analysis of static and dynamic postures (i.e. sitting, standing, gait, transfers, etc).The student will be able to identify deviation in gait based on video analysis to determine the potential problems that could cause the deviations.The student will be able to perform the appropriate clinical tests and measures learned in PT 7032 to identify impairments in body structure and function generated from posture and movement  (including gait) analyses.The student will be able to implement postural interventions that will make sitting for prolonged periods of time effective, efficient, and non-harmful for you and for patients/clients.The student will be able to instruct a patient or caregiver in appropriate body mechanics for bending and lifting activities.The student will be able to teach your classmates basic patient care skills through accurate demonstration and feedback.The student will be able to choose an appropriate assistive device for gait training and instruct a patient in appropriate use.The student will be able to demonstrate appropriate guarding techniques for assistive device and gait training.

Deals with application of physiological principles to the study of disease and injury, with particular attention to cellular injury, inflammation and repair, and immunity. Emphasis on implications of pathophysiology for physical therapy evaluation and treatment. General principles of pathophysiology will be applied to specific examples in class.  Subsequent courses in this curriculum will assume a working understanding of the concepts presented in this class. Will also prepare the student to treat patients with select systemic conditions, whether or not those conditions are the primary reason for physical therapy referral.  Emphasis will be placed on identification of the patient with systemic pathologies requiring further consultation or referral to other healthcare providers.   Requisites: PT 7011   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will accurately define terms associated with pathophysiological processes and use them appropriately.Students will compare and contrast the physiological mechanisms and clinical presentations of Type I and II diabetesStudents will define the various components of the immune system and how they function in concert in response to various mechanisms of injury.Students will describe how dysregulation of the immune system can lead to autoimmune and hypersensitivity disorders.Students will describe the biological processes underlying the development and spread of cancer.Students will describe the general function of cellular organelles and their contributions to cell function and homeostasis.Students will describe the pathway of hemostasis and identify the sites of dysfunction in disorders of hemostasis.Students will describe the physiological mechanisms contributing to various vascular disorders.Students will describe the sequence of events in the inflammatory response and their relation to cellular injury and repair.Students will differentially diagnose signs and symptoms of musculoskeletal origin (i.e., those within the PT scope of practice) from those of integumentary, vascular, immunological and neoplastic origins.Students will discuss signs, symptoms, and clinical presentation for persons affected with HIV and AIDS and their associated medication regimens.Students will explain how alterations in environment influence homeostasis and cell function.Students will explain how the pathophysiological changes associated with cancer contribute to signs and symptoms frequently observed in patients.Students will explain the processes governing the potential outcomes following various mechanisms of cellular injury (e.g., repair, regeneration, necrosis)Students will identify the physiological mechanisms, and describe their interactions in select examples of complex, multisystem diseases and conditions (e.g., diabetes, shock)Students will provide normal values for selected laboratory tests  and describe what deviations from these normal values indicate, with regard to the systems and pathologies covered in this course.

This survey course of medical physiology provides students with an overview of basic cellular processes and their impact in disease models in several key organ systems: integumentary, renal, genitourinary (GU), hepato-biliary, and gastro-intestinal (GI). In-depth examination of the physiology of diabetes is included as an example of a multi-system disorder. Emphasis is placed on the role of the physical therapist in applying signs and symptoms in the differential diagnosis of musculoskeletal conditions within the scope of PT practice from those arising from impairments of other systems.   Requisites: PT 7011 and PT 7012 and WARNING: No credit if taken after PT 7110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to define terms associated with disease processes and use them appropriately.The student will be able to apply knowledge of the general function of cellular organelles to overall cell function and homeostasis.The student will be able to apply the principles of intracellular signaling to human physiology, with particular emphasis on the endocrine system.The student will be able to describe the processes of transcription and translation and how they are regulated during both adaptive and maladaptive responses to stress.The student will be able to describe the sequence of events in the cellular response to tissue injury, integrating the hemostatic and inflammatory responses, and explain their relation to patient symptoms (e.g. pain, edema, fever). .The student will be able to describe the processes governing the potential outcomes following various mechanisms of cellular injury (e.g. repair, regeneration, adaptation, necrosis) and apply these data to prognoses following various types of injury.The student will be able to describe the biological processes underlying the development and spread of cancer and apply this knowledge to signs and symptoms frequently observed in patients with cancer.The student will be able to define the various components of the immune system and describe how they can both ward off and contribute to disease.The student will be able to describe normal integumentary anatomy and the processes associated with normal healing of integumentary injury.The student will be able to apply the principles of genetics, oncology, immunology and cell biology to the development and manifestation (including signs and symptoms and laboratory values) of the gastrointestinal system.The student will be able to apply principles of infectious disease to the manifestation, spread and treatment of select pathologies.The student will be able to apply the principles of genetics, oncology, immunology and cell biology to the development and manifestation (including signs and symptoms and laboratory values) of the renal system.The student will be able to explain how the pathophysiological changes associated with hemophilia and cancer including leukemia and sickle cell contribute to signs and symptoms frequently observed in patients.The student will be able to apply the principles of genetics, oncology, immunology and cell biology to the development and manifestation (including signs and symptoms and laboratory values) of the genitourinary system.The student will be able to demonstrate an understanding of how function of the digestive and renal systems influence the administration and metabolism of various drugs (e.g. pharmacokinetics).

This course provides the theoretical foundation for physical therapy evaluation and treatment of patients with cardiopulmonary conditions. Course content includes examination, evaluation of systems and clinical laboratory values, assessment and physiologic monitoring, discharge planning, determining patient equipment, and combating the effects of bed rest and deconditioning. Specific emphasis will be placed on evaluation, treatment, and management of the cardiovascular and pulmonary patient across all spectrums of care.   Requisites: PT 7111   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to compare and contrast normal cardiopulmonary anatomy and physiology with common cardiac and pulmonary conditions in order to extrapolate impairments.The student will be able to conduct an examination and evaluation of the pulmonary patient/client.The student will be able to interpret examination findings to inform treatment prescription in the cardiac and pulmonary patient.The student will be able to implement rehabilitation concepts to the patient with peripheral artery disease.The student will be able to identify normal and abnormal heart and lung sounds in order to assist with management of common cardiopulmonary disorders.The student will be able to prescribe appropriate bronchopulmonary hygiene for obstructive and restrictive pulmonary disease.The student will be able to evaluate an EKG rhythm strip in order to identify common cardiac arrhythmias.The student will be able to integrate knowledge of EKG characteristics with clinical signs and symptoms in order to inform physical therapy decisions.The student will be able to modify treatment of patients with cardiopulmonary diseases/disorders when contraindications to activity arise.The student will be able to describe medical management for cardiac and pulmonary conditions including surgical and non-surgical procedures.The student will be able to integrate knowledge of cardiac medical management into prescription of exercise and functional mobility.The student will be able to apply the phases of cardiac rehabilitation to the surgical and non-surgical cardiac patient/client.The student will be able to assess a patient’s cardiac or pulmonary condition in order to make appropriate recommendations for cardiac or pulmonary rehabilitation based on the current criteria for eligibility.The student will be able to assess the impact of cardiac and pulmonary medications on physiologic processes and physical therapy intervention.The student will be able to interpret arterial blood gas results to assist in determining appropriateness for initiation or modification of physical therapy.

course_name: Differential Diagnosis and Acute Care in Physical Therapy
description: Provides students with an overview of topics from a cellular to a systems level. Gastrointestinal, genitourinary, hepatobiliary, renal, endocrine, and metabolic systems will be covered. Additionally, the role of physical therapy in acute care and the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) will be covered. For each topic area or system, the student will be presented with the pathophysiology focused at the cellular and tissue level. The role of physical therapists in differential diagnosis, by recognizing the signs and symptoms associated with impairments of the systems, will be presented.  Prepares the student to identify the patient with systemic pathologies requiring further consultation or referral to other health care providers.   Requisites: PT 7111   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to interpret and extrapolate key information from a medical record in a timely fashion.The student will be able to survey the acute care environment for physiologic monitoring, precautions, barriers to safe movement and adjust courses of action appropriately during examination of the acute care patient.The student will be able to assess the impact of abnormal clinical laboratory values, vitals, images, and medical tests on designing or modifying exercise programs.The student will be able to evaluate the acute care patient with interpretation of the patient’s health condition(s), vitals signs, lab values, co-morbid conditions, medications, precautions/restrictions, and anticipated discharge/clinical course.The student will be able to demonstrate sound clinical reasoning and judgment in facilitation of discharge planning including but not limited to equipment needs, disposition, and therapy/activity recommendations.The student will be able to select appropriate outcome measures and screen for appropriateness for physical therapy in the acute care environment in order to demonstrate skilled physical therapy need.The student will be able to implement strategies to manage orthostatic hypotension.The student will be able to analyze the impact of bed rest and deconditioning on physiologic processes.The student will be able to evaluate and implement strategies to diagnose and prevent delirium.The student will be able to interpret basic cancer staging and physical therapy implications of medical intervention for various types of cancer.The student will be able to determine how physical functioning and tolerance to activity might be impacted in a patient experiencing dysfunction of the musculoskeletal, neuromuscular, cardiopulmonary, endocrine, renal, gastrointestinal and immune systems.The student will be able to integrate post-liver transplant precautions into clinical decision making in the acute care patient.The student will be able to describe surgical and non-surgical medical management of various medical conditions.The student will be able to integrate knowledge of referral pain patterns into the differential diagnostic process.The student will be able to appraise current literature to determine best course of action after new diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis.

Discussion of pharmacology and its implication in physical therapy is the focus. Emphasis is on drug classifications and drug mechanisms of action.   Requisites: PT 7111   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to break down and analyze classes of medication into pertinent details.The student will be able to explain significant drug interactions, adverse reactions, and side effects especially relevant to physical therapy.The student will be able to appraise illicit drug use concerns and details in physical therapy.The student will be able to analyze significant drug related problems based on patient demographics.The student will be able to evaluate a person’s medication list in relation to physical therapy treatment and patient safety.

Medical imaging course which covers plain x-ray, MRI, functional MRI, CT scan, positron emission tomography (PET) scan, and ultrasound as related to rehabilitation.   Requisites: Permission required and enrollment in a major within the College of Health Sciences and Professions.   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to recognize the background/history of the given imaging system.The student will be able to identify the basic technical functioning of the given imaging system.The student will be able to recognize the benefits and uses of the different imaging systems.The student will be able to select the imaging system/type used in a given image.The student will be able to discriminate normal and pathological (selected conditions) presentations on an image.The student will be able to recognize risks involved with the given imaging system.

course_name: Clinical and Professional Orientation in Physical Therapy
description: This course is designed to introduce students to some of the professional role responsibilities and the processes and requirements for clinical education experiences. Beginning with profession expectations and history of the profession, the course provides foundational information on physical therapy practice. The students will begin their Professional Development portfolio. The latter portion of the course is focused on preparing the student for clinical experiences in the curriculum.   Requisites: Admission to the PT program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Analyze different models of clinical education, including advantages/disadvantages of each, in order to maximize student’s future clinical education experiences.Create the framework for a Professional Development portfolio.Demonstrate basic competency with HIPAA regulations and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens training.Describe appropriate professional behavior utilizing the profession’s guiding documents including APTA Code of Ethics, APTA’s Core Values, and The Professional Behaviors for the 21st-century as reference.Describe the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model including its component parts and their application to patient care.Describe the history of the profession, including the evolution of professional organizations such as the APTA and FSBPT recognizing at least one means of personal involvement as a student physical therapist.Describe the process for selecting, preparing for, and completing both part- and full-time clinical education experiences.Utlize some of the profession’s core documents and tools as a mechanism for completing meaningful self-assessments and mentor/Clinical Instructor/clinic site evaluation.

course_name: Clinical and Professional Orientation in Physical Therapy
description: This course introduces students to professional role responsibilities and the profession’s core documents.  Clinical education processes and requirements are discussed. Health Insurance Portability & Accountability Act (HIPAA), Bloodborne Pathogens, and Tuberculosis Transmission and Prevention trainings are completed.  Foundational information related to legal, ethical, and professional behaviors, professional communication and cultural competence, and the history of the profession is provided.  Students are also introduced to the Program’s Professional Development Portfolio.   Requisites: Admission into the PT program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to describe appropriate professional behavior utilizing the profession’s guiding documents including the APTA Code of Ethics, APTA’s Core Values and The Professional Behaviors for the 21st Century.The student will be able to describe appropriate actions when given ethical, legal and reimbursement dilemmas utilizing core professional documents (i.e. Practice Act for the State of Ohio, APTA Code of Ethics, APTA Guide to PT Practice).The student will be able to describe the roles and interactions of physical therapists and other healthcare professionals across the continuum of care as a foundation for interprofessional education and practice.The student will be able to describe the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model including its component parts and their application to patient care.The student will be able to demonstrate basic competency with HIPAA regulations, Bloodborne Pathogens, and Tuberculosis Transmission and Prevention training.The student will be able to describe the Division of PT Policy and Procedures.The student will be able to analyze different models of clinical education, including advantages/disadvantages of each, in order to maximize student’s future clinical education experiences.The student will be able to utilize APTA’s core documents/tools including CPI, PT Student Evaluation for clinical education, core values/professional behavior tools as a mechanism for completing meaningful self-assessment and site evaluation.The student will be able to describe the Program’s Professional Development Portfolio and begin to develop a personal plan for meeting these expectations.The student will be able to describe the history of the profession, including the evolution of professional organizations such as the APTA and FSBPT recognizing at least one means of personal involvement as a student physical therapist.The student will be able to discuss cultural competence and the influence that culture has on communication, health/illness/disability beliefs, and behaviors.The student will be able to describe strategies that can be used for effective and culturally competent communication and education in the design and delivery of patient centered care.The student will be able to identify resources and use them to learn about the demographics and cultural considerations of a population to be served in furture clinical rotations and practice.

Provides foundational information on physical therapy practice including history, roles and responsbilities within the continuum of care and emphasizes professional communication, documentation skills, cultural competency, and educational practices for clients and families.   Requisites: PT 7030   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will accurately describe the levels of care and compare the roles/responsibilities of physical therapists in these different practice settings.The student will analyze patient education materials for content, cultural competency, and clarity.The student will define and use medical terms and abbreviations in verbal communication and documentation.The student will define cultural competence and discuss the influence that culture has on communication, health/illness/disability beliefs and behaviors.The student will demonstrate competency with HIPAA regulations, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens training, the Practice Act for the State of Ohio, APTA Code of Ethics, APTA Core Values, and Generic Abilities to identify appropriate professional behavior.The student will describe a physical therapist’s fiduciary responsibility to patients.The student will describe the heterogeneity within a cultural group and the need to avoid stereotyping while studying documented generalizations about specific cultures in order to communicate effectively and to provide optimal clinical care.The student will describe the history of the profession, including the evolution of professional organizations such as the American Physical Therapy Association and the Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy.The student will design and implement effective instruction about a patient’s current condition, intervention strategies, home exercise programs, caregiver training needs, and community based risk factor reduction.The student will document physical therapy initial examinations, daily notes, progress notes, and discharge summaries with a functional outcome perspective that can be adapted to variety of documentation formats.The student will evaluate how one’s own personal culture and general assumptions of the US healthcare system influence delivery of clinical care.The student will identify questions that will elicit information about a patient, caregiver, or community’s educational needs, readiness to learn, learning style, and potential barriers to learning.The student will identify questions that will elicit information about a specific patient’s cultural background, communication preferences, health beliefs/behaviors and explanatory model about their reason for seeking physical therapy services.The student will identify resources and use them to learn about the demographics and cultural considerations of a population to be served in future clinical rotations and practice.The student will use medical record documentation in the appropriate style that is concise, accurate, clear and meets legal, regulatory, and reimbursement criteria.The student will use professional documents such as, the Ohio Practice Act , APTA Code of Ethics, APTA Core Values and the Generic Abilities to identify appropriate professional behavior and guide one’s own professional development.The student will write concrete, measurable, patient-centered goals that integrate the disablement spectrum/ICF model impairment/body structure function, functional limitation/activity, disability/participation and that are integrated to each other.The student will write physical therapy assessments, diagnoses, and prognoses that synthesize clinical data and reflect clinical reasoning and decision making.

course_name: Professional Communication and Documentation in PT
description: This course will focus on the development of professional written and oral communication skills, documentation skills, cultural competency, and educational practices for clients and families related to the practice of physical therapy.   Requisites: PT 7300 or 7301   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to use medical terminology and abbreviations in communication and documentation.The student will be able to communicate pertinent health information effectively and efficiently with health care professionals to improve patient centered care.The student will be able to implement strategies for effective and culturally competent patient education appropriate to the learning style and needs of the patient.The student will be able to implement strategies for effective communication with patients/families/healthcare providers/Physical Therapist Assistants/peers in simple and difficult situations/scenarios.The student will be able to adjust verbal and non-verbal communication in a time sensitive and professional manner in response to consequences of his/her actions with patients/healthcare providers/peers.The student will be able to demonstrate professional communication and behaviors while assessing and evaluating peers.The student will be able to identify the implications of incident reporting and its impact on risk management.The student will be able to analyze legal practice standards as it pertains to state and federal regulations on documentation.The student will be able to explain the purpose(s) of medical documentation.The student will be able to identify types of information consistent with various sections of physical therapy documentation.The student will be able to complete medical record documentation in the appropriate style that meets legal, regulatory, and reimbursement criteria.The student will be able to document physical therapy subjective and objective sections in various documentation formats and styles.The student will be able to compose physical therapy assessments, diagnoses, and prognoses utilizing clinical data and reflect clinical reasoning and decision-making.The student will be able to create SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time bound) physical therapy goals.

Principles of evidence based practice will be discussed. Topics covered will be forms and hierarchy of evidence, searches using a variety of databases pertinent to physical therapy, formulating the research question, measurement, and basic research design.  Emphasis will be placed on understanding and utilization of statistical methods as well as on acquiring the skills to critically analyze research.   Requisites: Admission to the PT program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to appraise research questions for appropriateness in descriptive and experimental designs.The student will be able to develop a searchable clinical question using PICO (Patient, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) format.The student will be able to analyze sampling techniques used in rehabilitation research as it pertains to research validity and generalizability.The student will be able to interpret measures of central tendency and variance used in descriptive results.The student will be able to choose appropriate statistical designs based on study question and design.The student will be able to interpret descriptive and inferential study results and statistical significance.The student will be able to differentiate between statistical significance and clinical relevance.The student will be able to apply an understanding of reliability for tests and measures as it applies to research validity and clinical practice.The student will be able to differentiate between different components of validity.The student will be able to develop a “Clinical Bottom Line” from a rehabilitation research article.The student will be able to apply the components of an evidence-based approach to patient care.The student will be able to differentiate between sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and likelihood ratios.The student will be able to apply the results of a diagnostic test in regards to its ability to alter post-test odds.The student will be able to apply odds ratios and relative risk ratios to development of a patient prognosis.The student will be able to interpret estimates of magnitude(i.e. effect size) for selected interventions.The student will be able to differentiate between common qualitative research designs.

Neuroanatomical study of the human brain, brainstem, cranial nerves, and spinal cord is covered emphasizing function and clinical considerations relative to physical therapy.   Requisites: PT 7011 and PT 7012   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture, 2.0 laboratory  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to outline the developmental origin of the human nervous system, emphasizing the neural plate, neural tube and neural crest cells.The student will be able to categorize neural subdivisions of both anatomical and functional relationships as well as histological and morphological neural subtypes.The student will be able to describe how the human brain is sectioned both anatomically and functionally.The student will be able to illustrate an overview of the surface anatomy of both the brain as well as the brainstem and spinal cord.The student will be able to identify the major sources and patterns of vascular supply to the central nervous system.The student will be able to relate both the anatomical and physiological characteristics of electrical signaling and chemical transmission.The student will be able to demonstrate understanding of the anatomical and functional components of the peripheral nervous system.The student will be able to identify the characteristics of sensory detection for peripheral stimuli including pain responses.The student will be able to classify spinal cord anatomy as well as develop a working knowledge of both ascending and descending neural pathways.The student will be able to apply neuroanatomical knowledge to pathological processes associated with both the central and peripheral nervous systems.

course_name: Neural Basis of Movement I: Systems and Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Covers a systems approach to neural basis of motor, sensory, cognitive, affective, and homeostatic processes that underlies behavior with emphasis on the motor control and motor learning of locomotion, postural control/balance, and skilled movement. Students will apply content to evaluating neural origins of movement dysfunction and the physiological basis for strategies to improve skilled motor performance.   Requisites: PT 7500   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to explain the physiological basis of electrical and chemical mechanisms associated with synaptic activity and chemical transmission.The student will be able to analyze the anatomy and function of the autonomic nervous system including peripheral mechanisms and central control.The student will be able to outline neural control of bowel, bladder and sexual function.The student will be able to differentiate between the physiological mechanisms underlying normal and pathologic pain perception.The student will be able to examine the function of the sensorimotor cortices, cerebellum, basal ganglia and spinal cord.The student will be able to explain neural control mechanisms of consciousness, attention and emotion.The student will be able to organize functional contributions of the neural axis relative to different categories of movement.The student will be able to describe the mechanisms of neural plasticity associated with peripheral and central nervous systems.The student will be able to prescribe intervention procedures based on motor learning principles.

course_name: Physical Therapy Mgt of Brain Injury and Balance Disorders
description: Focuses on utilizing knowledge of neuroanatomy, motor control systems and motor learning concepts to the physical therapy examination, and evaluation and treatment of persons who have focal or diffuse lesions within the brain, such as stroke or traumatic brain injury.  Focus is on a systems approach to clinical decision-making, functional retraining and case management.   Requisites: PT 7510   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture, 4.0 laboratory  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Given a patient history, the student will identify risk factors for stroke, strategies for risk reduction as part of the screening process, and need for referral.The student will critically evaluate treatment theories and clinical translation of those theories into treatment interventions to alleviate impairments, movement dysfunction and disability.The student will design functional activities for simulated patients for use outside of the clinical environment that are consistent with the attainment of functional goals.The student will determine from examination and evaluation effective evidence-based treatment interventions for remediation of the identified impairments and functional limitations.The student will determine from examination and evaluation primary and secondary pathologies, impairments, functional limitations and disability for a particular patient model.The student will determine from examination and evaluation the need for adaptive and assistive equipment, supportive or positioning systems.The student will determine from examination and evaluation the physical therapy diagnosis, prognosis and goal setting for a particular patient model that will guide the use of interventions.The student will determine from examination, evaluation and diagnostic procedures a prioritization of patient problems, especially those most amenable to physical therapy intervention.The student will document accurately and completely the results of the examination, assessment and intervention as well as the patient’s response to treatment.The student will educate patient with risk factors about signs/symptoms of stroke and how to access available acute medical management to minimize stroke severity.The student will perform select interventions for BPPV, unilateral and bilateral hypofunctioning, and motion sensitivity in patients with balance/vestibular disorders according to the best evidence.The student will perform selected examination, evaluation, and treatment procedures for those patients complaining of loss of balance or vertigo.The student will perform selected physical therapy evaluation and intervention procedures that focus on functional outcomes given the impairments, functional limitations, and movement dysfunction of the patient.The student will predict clinical signs and symptoms when presented with a specific focal or diffuse brain injury based on location, blood vessels involved or other pathology.The student will recognize the signs/symptoms of a brain attack and the relevance to acute medical management time frames to use for patient education and prevention.The student will sustain ethical relationships with colleagues, the health care team, clients, families, equipment vendors and payers.The student will utilize patient resources effectively in the setting in which the patient is seen.The student will utilize strategies for intervention that take into account the patient’s executive and cognitive abilities to assure the best outcomes.The student will utilize task-oriented observational movement analysis to identify critical elements of functional movement that are lacking and to generate hypotheses regarding contributing impairments.

course_name: Foundations for Management of Adult Stroke and Brain Injury in Physical Therapy
description: This course applies the knowledge of neuroanatomy and motor control systems to the physical therapy management of movement dysfunction which results from a focal or diffuse lesion, such as stroke or brain injury, in the central nervous system. Course content introduces the foundational characteristics and  clinical presentation of focal and diffuse brain lesions, evidence-based systems approach to examination and assessment, and critical evaluation of treatment theory.   Requisites: PT 7500 and PT 7510   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to critically evaluate neurorehabilitation theoretical approaches and the clinical translation of those theories into treatment interventions to alleviate impairments, movement dysfunction and disability after neurological insult.The student will be able to summarize the epidemiology, etiology and pathophysiology of various neurologic insults.The student will be able to identify clinical presentation to determine pathological processes/neurological injury site.The student will be able to compare evaluation data to determine screen, referral, or restorative, compensatory or preventative treatment interventions.The student will be able to appraise neurological medical information to determine acute medical management and prognosis of various neurological insults.The student will be able to distinguish primary from secondary impairments and their impact movement dysfunction.The student will be able to construct explanations that indicate understanding of how cognitive and behavioral issues impact treatment interventions.The student will be able to deconstruct how social determinants of health impact the diagnosis and treatment of the neurologic insult.The student will be able to scrutinize decision-making processes for behaviors of cultural competence and cultural humility.The student will be able to choose the appropriate continuum of care placement based on diagnosis, prognosis and social determinants of health.

course_name: Clinical Applications for Management of Adult Stroke and Brain Injury in Physical Therapy
description: Course content addresses the synthesis and application of didactic knowledge regarding clinical presentation of focal and diffuse brain lesions and movement dysfunctions after neurological insult. Course emphasizes the effective performance of a physical therapy examination and assessment.  Design and implementation of task-specific and activity based prevention and interventions with the goal of promoting optimal functional recovery and neural reorganization is also covered.   Requisites: PT 7500 and PT 7510   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to alter the standard neurologic examination format to accommodate patient/diagnosis/ impairment/caregiver availability/time.The student will be able to select the appropriate outcome measures to assess impairment at the structure/function and activity level to alleviate movement dysfunction and prevent secondary complications.The student will be able to effectively illustrate proficiency during implementation of assessment procedures to determine the level of impairment at the function and activity level to alleviate movement dysfunction and prevent secondary complications.The student will be able to evaluate examination data to generate a physical therapy problem list, assessment/diagnosis, prognosis (including discharge planning) that addresses the impairments and movement dysfunction.The student will be able to select the appropriate treatment interventions to address impairments at the structure/function and activity level to alleviate movement dysfunction and prevent secondary complications.The student will be able to effectively illustrate proficiency during implementation of treatment interventions to address impairment at the structure/function and activity level to alleviate movement dysfunction and prevent secondary complications.The student will be able to demonstrate treatment interventions that serve to strengthen and modify tone/spasticity in muscle groups, increase joint range of motion and muscle length, and options for independent motor skill practice by the patient.The student will be able to adjust neurologic functional skills based on social determinants of health/cultural norms and impairments requiring verbal, tactile or demonstrative cues.The student will be able to create a treatment plan based upon available clinical evidence and/or relevant theory that addresses assessment/diagnosis underlying the functional limitations and  movement dysfunction.The student will be able to demonstrate behaviors of cultural competence and humility during the evaluation or treatment process.

course_name: Balance and Vestibular Conditions in Physical Therapy
description: Students will apply knowledge of motor control and motor learning theory to the physical therapy assessment and treatment of persons who have acute, chronic and/or degenerative neurologic conditions of the nervous system with an emphasis on the evaluation and treatment of balance and vestibular disorders in the context of central and peripheral lesions.   Requisites: PT 7500 and 7510   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to analyze balance dysfunction in order to identify the contributing impairments for plan of care development.The student will be able to display proficiency in balance outcome measure administration.The student will be able to interpret outcome measure scores to inform assessment and POC.The student will be able to teach relevant anatomy and physiology of the vestibular system as it relates to impairments and functional limitations in patient friendly language.The student will be able to demonstrate the oculomotor exam.The student will be able to interpret oculomotor findings for differential diagnosis of central versus peripheral signs of vestibular pathology.The student will be able to select the most appropriate subjective interview questions to assist with differential diagnosis of the patient with dizziness.The student will be able to conduct a subjective interview specific to balance and vestibular dysfunction in order to utilize the most appropriate objective measures in time efficient fashion.The student will be able to determine appropriateness of delegation of physical therapy vestibular intervention to physical therapist assistants.The student will be able to evaluate basic dysfunction in a patient with dizziness as it relates to these diagnoses: benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, peripheral hypofunctioning, central dysfunction, motion sensitivity, and balance dysfunction.The student will be able to select appropriate treatment measures for benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, peripheral hypofunctioning, central dysfunction, motion sensitivity, and balance dysfunction.The student will be able to effectively implement treatments for benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, peripheral hypofunctioning, central dysfunction, motion sensitivity, and balance dysfunction.The student will be able to identity red flags during a balance and/or vestibular examination that require a referral to a physician.The student will be able to appraise clinical presentation of vestibular dysfunction in order to determine prognosis.

course_name: Physical Therapy Management of Chronic and/or Progressive Disorders
description: Applies knowledge of motor control and motor learning theory to the assessment and treatment of patients with chronic and/or progressive disorders.  Focus is on a systems approach to clinical decision-making and case management.   Requisites: PT 7520   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture, 4.0 laboratory  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will apply principles of motor learning to support the best outcomes in patients with chronic and/or progressive disorders.Students will critically analyze the literature related to examination and treatment interventions related to chronic/progressive disorders.Students will demonstrate examination procedures specific to patients with spinal cord injury and other chronic disorders.Students will demonstrate, perform, and teach functional skills training per level of injury or disease progression.Students will determine a prognosis for care and identify several long and short term goals for the patient’s program.Students will evaluate examination data to generate a physical therapy diagnosis that identifies contributing impairments to the presenting movement dysfunction.Students will identify and address educational needs of the patient, family, or caregivers through written and verbal communication.Students will organize an examination including the history and physical examination and identify specific tests and measures pertinent to the underlying pathology.Students will plan for the discharge of a patient including selection of adaptive/assistive equipment, wheelchairs and services.Students will select outcome measures for the patient with chronic disorders that have reliability, validity, and sensitivity to change.Students will select procedural interventions that are impairment and function-based to alleviate movement dysfunction.Students will develop and demonstrate a program to strengthen muscle groups (including PNF), increase joint range of motion and muscle length.

course_name: Foundations for Management of Chronic and/or Progressive Disability in Physical Therapy
description: Course presents knowledge of acute disease onset or disease progression, motor control and motor learning to the assessment and management of patients with chronic and/or progressive disease or injury of the spinal cord or brain.  The course stresses the importance of timely intervention and prevention of secondary impairments, functional limitations, and disability over the course of illness or disease.   Requisites: PT 7521 and 7522   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to summarize the epidemiology, etiology and pathogenesis of spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular diseases.The student will be able to describe contemporary diagnostic and medical management procedures for spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular diseases.The student will be able to outline impact of spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular disease on body systems.The student will be able to identify activity and participation limitations associated with spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular diseases.The student will be able to categorize clinical presentation associated with spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular diseases using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model.The student will be able to evaluate key prognostic indicators associated with patient presentation following spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular diseases.The student will be able to explain preventative, restorative and compensatory treatment approach theory for spinal cord injury and other chronic/progressive neuromuscular diseases.The student will be able to modify a therapeutic exercise program based on underlying physiological basis of weakness.The student will be able to relate social determinants of health and cultural factors to effective rehabilitation management.

course_name: Clinical Applications for Patients with Chronic and/or Progressive Disability in Physical Therapy
description: Application of didactic knowledge of disease progression and clinical presentation to the assessment and management of patients with chronic and/or progressive disease or injury of the spinal cord or brain. Emphasis is placed on appropriate timing of recovery versus compensatory interventions for the purpose of retraining functional mobility. Students develop proficiency in the performance of evaluation and treatment techniques.   Requisites: PT 7521 and 7522   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will be able to design an effective physical therapy examination based on client history and underlying medical condition(s).The student will be able to demonstrate proficiency during implementation of examination procedures.The student will be able to formulate a physical therapy diagnosis and prognosis based on examination data and level of neurological injury/disease progression.The student will be able to prescribe appropriate treatment interventions to address deficits at the structure/function and activity level to alleviate movement dysfunction and prevent secondary complications.The student will be able to create a comprehensive written plan of care including patient-centered short and long-term goals in SMART format, relevant ICD-10 CPT codes, individualized client education, and coordination of appropriate referral sources.The student will be able to adjust treatment approach (prevention/restoration/compensation) to level of neurological injury/disease progression .The student will be able to propose alternative rehabilitative strategies based on social determinants of health and cultural factors.The student will be able to display behaviors of cultural competence and cultural humility during client interaction.

Integrates knowledge and skills from previous and concomitant courses to solve complex clinical problems related to neuromusculoskeletal disorders under the guidance of faculty mentors. Incorporates evidence based practice for examination, evaluation, and intervention strateges for selected patients.   Requisites: PT 7530   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 laboratory, 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  The student will conduct a literature search to determine evidence basis for the treatment plan suggested and write a critical appraisal of current evidence.The student will critique case presentations in class orally and in writing.The student will develop a prognosis that includes an overall anticipated outcome and time frame for the presenting problems.The student will develop the skills needed for lifelong learning and professional interaction with peers.The student will evaluate data gathered during the examination to form a physical therapy diagnosis that will guide the treatment plan.The student will identify relevant functional problems and list hypotheses as to why the problem exists.The student will participate in peer review through assessment of seminar/synthesis facilitators and discussants.The student will present the case study to colleagues.The student will select with an appropriate rationale, competently implement and interpret relevant screening measures, tests and measures to gather data pertinent to the patient problem.The student will use evaluation findings to write goals and a treatment plan.The student will write treatment goals and implement a treatment plan that addresses the patient’s impairments, functional limitations, and disabilities.

Students will be introduced to the theoretical constructs for the use of physical agents in the treatment of patients by physical therapists.  Additionally, students will practice the application of both thermal and electric physical agents in the treatment and rehabilitation of orthopedic, neurological, and integumentary conditions.   Requisites: PT 7110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture, 3.0 laboratory  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will apply common techniques for the treatment of lymphedema.Students will define the role of physical therapy in the management of the burn patient.Students will demonstrate an understanding of the basic pathophysiology associated with non-healing chronic wounds of different etiologies.Students will describe pathophysiological causes of lymphedema.Students will describe the mechanisms underlying therapeutic interventions for treating chronic wounds and the prognoses associated with these interventions.Students will describe the physiological effects of electro-therapeutic physical agents on both healthy and impaired tissues.Students will describe the physiological effects of thermal agents on both healthy and impaired tissues.Students will describe the role of physical agents in pain modulation.Students will describe the role of physical agents in rehabilitation of the neuromuscular system.Students will describe the role of physical agents in tissue repair.Students will determine the most appropriate physical agent to utilize for a given case so as to maximize effectiveness of therapeutic interventions.Students will examine issues of safety associated with both thermal and electro-therapeutic physical agents.Students will safely apply the physical agents utilized most frequently by physical therapists.Students will use existing scientific literature to guide treatment of a given patient condition.

The physical agents typically used in a physical therapy clinical environment are covered.  The biophysics of thermal and electro-therapeutic agents will be discussed. Emphasis will be placed on clinical decision making and psychomotor skills required to apply these physical agents in a safe and effective manner.
