Student is able to reason and develop an argument in supporting sections of an essay.Student is able to identify, compare, and analyze information from multiple textual sources and is able to synthesize information from various sources to solve problems and perform writing tasks.Student: recognizes text-based paraphrase and understands its purpose, recognizes references, acknowledgements, and bibliographic citations, and is able to identify, compare, and analyze information from multiple textual sources.Student: uses textual evidence to verify comprehension and support his/her position and demonstrates ability to infer meaning within a text, to distinguish fact from opinion, and to detect author’s point-of-view.

In this course, students explore the history and development of the physician assistant (PA) profession, professional, ethical and legal issues affecting clinical practice, and the PA’s role in the healthcare system.   Requisites: Admission to the Ohio University Physician Assistant Program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:   Students will be able to analyze the significance of current issues in the health care including US health care delivery system, healthcare policy, public health issues, and political arenas that impact the PA profession.Students will be able to articulate the continuing medical education (CME) requirements for the PA.Students will be able to define and discuss professionalism in PA practice.Students will be able to describe the role of the PA as a member of the healthcare team.Students will be able to describe the role of the Supervising Physician and the dynamics of the PA/physician relationship.Students will be able to discuss approach to patient safety, quality improvement, prevention of medical errors, and risk management.Students will be able to discuss cultural diversity within the PA Profession.Students will be able to discuss regulations governing PA practice, credentialing, licensure, and malpractice.Students will be able to discuss the certification and recertification process for state licensure and NCCPA certification.Students will be able to discuss the impact of reimbursement policies on PA practice.Students will be able to discuss the principals of Osteopathy.Students will be able to discuss the use of evidence-based medicine and information literacy in professional practice.Students will be able to evaluate employment and leadership opportunities for the PA.Students will be able to explain the important roles that PA’s play in providing care to the medically under served.Students will be able to explain the significant milestones in the development of the PA profession.Students will be able to identify and discuss the various ethical issues confronting the PA in professional practice.Students will be able to identify commonly used acronyms, abbreviations and terminology used in the PA profession.

course_name: Physician Assistant Practice II: US Healthcare Systems and Policy
description: The second in a series of two courses, students will explore the U.S. health system, regulations and policies that affect the delivery of healthcare in the United States.   Requisites: PA 5110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Analyze the significance of current issues in the health care and political arenas that impact the PA profession.Articulate key concepts in the US Health care policy making process.Describe the intricacies of US health care delivery system.Describe the role of accreditation agencies within the healthcare system.Discuss racial and ethnic health care disparities.Discuss regulations governing PA practice, credentialing, licensure and malpractice.Discuss the impact of US health care policy on clinical practice.Discuss the implications regarding laboratory safety and state and federal governmental regulations and standards.Explain the relationship between US health care policy and public health.

course_name: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention for the Physician Assistant
description: This course is designed to prepare the physician assistant student with the knowledge and skills to apply principles of health promotion and disease prevention to diverse patient populations in a variety of clinical and community settings.   Requisites: PA 5110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to apply the principles of health promotion and disease prevention to the development of patient education strategies to risk behaviors (such as obesity, smoking, sexual practices, nutrition, etc).Students will be able to differentiate among screening tools for health risks in patients and communities.Students will be able to discuss and differentiate the stages of behavior change theory.Students will be able to discuss common health risks in selected patient populations.Students will be able to distinguish between the health risks of individual patients, families, and communities.Students will be able to include a consideration of  social, cultural, and economic issues in patient education strategies.

course_name: Concepts of Leadership and Management for the Physician Assistant
description: This course provides students with the foundation to understand and appreciate leadership and management principles necessary to assume leadership positions in the Physician Assistant (PA) profession and clinical practice.  Students will examine and critically analyze current leadership skills, theories and management principles in health care organizations.   Requisites: PA 5110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to analyze and describe labor force demographics and trends in PA workforce diversity.Students will be able to analyze and describe the determinants of employee job satisfaction, turnover, and commitment.Students will be able to categorize various team structures and discuss strategies to evaluate team effectiveness.Students will be able to compare and contrast the differences between leadership and management.Students will be able to define workplace harassment and articulate steps for prevention.Students will be able to describe and give examples of the traditional classifications of management and the leadership skills necessary for working in healthcare teams.Students will be able to describe how stewardship applies to those in the healthcare leadership roles.Students will be able to describe opportunities for professional and leadership development for health care team members.Students will be able to describe the importance of ethics, integrity and trust in clinical practice and give examples of the effects that each has on establishing and maintaining inter-professional relationships.Students will be able to explain resolution strategies for inter-personal conflict between healthcare team members, patients and their families.Students will be able to perform a self-assessment and evaluate personal strengths, skills, and challenges when faced with leadership and management responsibilities.

This course introduces students to foundational professional and leadership principles within health organizations and clinical practice. Students explore key aspects of professional identity emphasizing self-assessment relating to leadership traits and skills along with needed professional behavior characteristics essential for success in PA practice.   Requisites: PA 5110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to analyze different leadership types and apply those to transformational leadership principles in clinical and professional settings.Students will be able to analyze personal leader types in comparison to organizational leadership development.Students will be able to evaluate strategies for leadership resilience that include stress management, adapting to challenges, and informed decision-making.Students will be able to apply the situational analysis model when assessing clinical and professional scenarios to make informed decisions.Students will be able to describe the effects of individual leadership behaviors on healthcare teams and organizations.Students will be able to design an effective professional CV and cover letter that effectively highlights skills, education, certifications, and leadership experience.Students will be able to develop a strong online professional presence through social media platforms, such as LinkedIn to enhance networking and career advancement.Students will be able to describe potential career pathways, including direct employment, fellowship training, and clinical roles.

course_name: Professional Development: Certification and Practice for the Physician Assistant
description: This course will assist students in the application of concepts and knowledge gained from didactic instruction and clinical rotations in preparation for graduation, certification, licensure, professional employment and clinical practice.   Requisites: PA 5110   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to articulate the certification process through the NCCPA including initial certification and recertification examinations.Students will be able to articulate the requirements for institutional credentialing and privileging.Students will be able to discuss financial compensation, benefits, and contract negotiation.Students will be able to discuss strategies for gainful employment and develop a CV.Students will be able to explain physician assistant practice laws and regulation.Students will be able to explain the process for state credentialing, registration, and licensure application.Students will be able to explain the types of medical malpractice and risk management strategies.Students will be able to successfully complete all program summative written and practical exams.

This course builds on principles of professionalism and leadership skills and focuses on career development, personal growth, and leadership within health systems and the physician assistant profession. Students refine their professional identity and develop a career plan, including job portfolio creation, job search strategies, and long-term career goals. Students also learn how personal leadership traits and values contribute to organizational transformation.   Requisites: PA 5141   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to develop a personal and professional leadership vision, aligning career aspirations with long-term goals in clinical practice and healthcare leadership.Students will be able to apply self-reflection and feedback mechanisms to continuously improve professional competencies and leadership capabilities using frameworks such as SWOT analysis.Students will be able to design a strategic career plan that outlines short-term and long-term objectives, considering specialization, employment opportunities, leadership development and professional growth.Students will be able to effectively communicate in conflict resolution and team collaboration in clinical settings.Students will be able to develop a plan of action for implementing future vision, leadership traits, and leadership behaviors that lead to professional growth.Students will be able to analyze how innovation and change management contribute to improving clinical practice and healthcare systems.Students will be able to analyze the state-specific licensing requirements for physician assistants and navigate the application process for licensure in various states.Students will be able to describe potential PA career pathways, including direct employment, fellowship training, and advanced clinical roles.

Provides a foundation of knowledge in the technology, application, ordering and interpretation of diagnostic imaging which will be applied in the practice of evidence-based medicine.   Requisites: Admission to the Ohio University Physician Assistant Program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 1.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to select the appropriate diagnostic imaging for common medical conditions.Students will be able to articulate the standardized methods of the interpretation of radiologic imaging.Students will be able to identify normal anatomy on common radiologic imaging.Students will be able to differentiate between normal and abnormal radiologic findings in each organ system.

course_name: Clinical Gross Anatomy for the Physician Assistant
description: This physician assistant course in human gross anatomy provides foundational concepts in the structure and function of the human body. The course includes lecture and laboratory including dissection and prosection of human cadaveric specimens to focus on the clinical application of human anatomy to health and disease.   Requisites: Admission into the Physician Assistant program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture, 6.0 laboratory  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to apply principles of normal anatomy and anatomical pathology to health and disease.Students will be able to discuss and differentiate anatomic structure and function by location and relationship.Students will be able to identify anatomic landmarks and relationships utilizing correct terminology and spelling.Students will be able to identify selected anatomic structures on radiographs, using a systematic approach.Students will be able to use critical problem solving to address patient scenarios.

course_name: Clinical Pathophysiology I for the Physician Assistant
description: The first in a series of three courses for physician assistant students, this course provides foundational content in physiology and pathophysiology as it relates to cell function, homeostasis and molecular interactions within the human body.   Requisites: Admission to the Ohio University Physician Assistant Program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to apply physiological principles to the pathophysiological processes that can develop within selected body systems.Students will be able to demonstrate critical thinking to apply knowledge of physiology and pathophysiology to health and disease states.Students will be able to describe and differentiate between the normal physiology and pathophysiological processes.Students will be able to discuss and differentiate the physiologic changes with aging over the lifespan.

course_name: Clinical Pathophysiology I for Physician Assistants
description: The first in a series of three courses in clinical pathophysiology. Focuses on the foundational physiologic and pathophysiologic processes as they relate to cell function, homeostasis, and molecular interactions within the human body. Disease processes include the body’s response to acute inflammation and hemorrhage, thrombosis and embolism, allergic reactions, neoplasms and infections.   Requisites: Admission into the Physician Assistant program   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 2.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to discuss homeostatic processes that ensure normal physiologic functioning of major organ systems.Students will be able to describe differences in homeostatic and physiological functioning as they relate to disease onset across the lifespan including inflammation and hemorrhage, thrombosis and embolism, allergic reactions, neoplasms and infection.Students will be able to demonstrate critical thinking in their understanding of the etiologies and pathophysiological processes related to disease processes including acute inflammation and hemorrhage, thrombosis and embolism, and allergic reactions.Students will be able to discuss the body’s pathophysiological response to disease including acute inflammation and hemorrhage, thrombosis and embolism, allergic reactions, neoplasms and infections. .

course_name: Clinical Pathophysiology II for the Physician Assistant
description: The second in a series of three courses for physician assistant students, this course provides foundational content in physiology and pathophysiology to include the function of cells, tissues, organs and organ systems in health and disease states. Course topics include the following systems: Integumentary, Immune, Neurologic, musculoskeletal, hematology and oncology.   Requisites: PA 5220   Repeat/Retake Information: May not be retaken.  Lecture/Lab Hours: 3.0 lecture  Grades: Eligible Grades: A-F,PR,WP,WF,WN,FN,AU,I  Learning Outcomes:  Students will be able to apply physiological principles to the pathophysiological processes that can develop within selected body systems.Students will be able to demonstrate critical thinking to apply knowledge of physiology and pathophysiology to health and disease states in selected body systems.Students will be able to describe and differentiate between the normal physiology and pathophysiological processes of selected body systems.Students will be able to discuss and differentiate the physiologic changes with aging over the lifespan.Students will be able to discuss the clinical presentation, including symptoms and signs, of selected pathophysiological processes and disease states in adults.

course_name: Clinical Pathophysiology II for Physician Assistants
description: The second in a series of three courses in clinical pathophysiology.
